summary: Backend regression after CRITICAL loyalty diamond credit fix. ALL 18/18 tests PASS (16 pre-existing + 2 regression tests for the bug). The ObjectId coercion fix in PUT /api/online-orders/{id}/status (server.py ~line 2562) is verified working: customer_id (str on order doc) is now wrapped with ObjectId() before db.customers.update_one — diamond_balance increments by diamonds_earned exactly once and a loyalty_transactions row is written. Idempotency on a second status=delivered call also confirmed (no double-credit). The same ObjectId coercion on the reward redemption path at order creation (server.py ~line 2396) is verified by the new TestRewardRedemptionDeduction test: cost_diamonds is properly deducted from customer balance when reward_id is supplied. Defensive logger.warning when modified_count==0 is in place but did NOT fire (correct — credit succeeded). 16 previously-passing tests still pass, no regression.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix verified: server.py PUT /online-orders/{id}/status now coerces customer_id with ObjectId() before find_one/update_one (lines ~2562-2570). Defensive logger.warning at line 2601 will surface future silent-failure regressions.
Reward redemption path at line 2394-2399 also correctly coerces cust['_id'] to ObjectId before update_one. The try/except around ObjectId coercion is good defensive coding for legacy str IDs.

Underlying type drift NOT fixed (cust['_id'] is still mutated to str by get_current_customer at line 2120-2123, and order docs still store the str). The ObjectId coercion is now applied at every db.customers query site that matters, but this remains a footgun for future code. Consider keeping cust['_id'] as ObjectId internally and only stringify in API responses — but this is a refactor, not blocking.
loyalty_transactions row is written ONLY after successful modified_count>0 — correct, prevents orphan tx logs. Good.
compute_business_hours_status still doesn't support overnight hours (e.g. 18:00 -> 02:00). MVP-acceptable, already noted in code.

rca of the issue: Original bug: customer_id stored as str on order doc but customers._id is ObjectId, so update_one matched 0 docs and silently skipped credit. Fix verified working: ObjectId() wrap on both find_one and update_one in PUT /online-orders/{id}/status (delivery path) and in POST /online-orders (reward redemption path). Defensive logger.warning added when modified_count==0. Reproduction now PASSES end-to-end.
